Load domain files and return them

Source: R/get_data.r
ks_get_data.Rd

Reads one or more data files from path and returns them as tibbles. A single-domain call returns a tibble; a multi-domain call returns a named list of tibbles (names are the lowercased domain names).

Usage

ks_get_data(
  ...,
  path = getOption("path.data", "."),
  type = c("auto", "rds", "xpt", "xlsx", "csv", "csvks"),
  xpt_reader = getOption("kstools.xpt.reader", "haven")
)

Arguments

...

Unquoted (or quoted) domain names, e.g. dm, ae, lb.

path

Directory containing the data files. Defaults to getOption("path.data", ".").

type

File type: "auto" (detect from extension), "rds", "xpt", "xlsx", "csv", or "csvks" (CSV with KeyStat comment metadata).

xpt_reader

Reader to use for .xpt files: "haven" (default) or "internal" (use ks_read_xpt). Defaults to getOption("kstools.xpt.reader", "haven").

Value

For a single domain, a tibble. For two or more domains, a named list of tibbles keyed by the lowercased domain name.

Details

Supported formats: .rds (R native), .xpt (SAS XPORT), .xlsx (Microsoft Excel), .csv (plain CSV), .csv with KeyStat comments (type = "csvks").

Domain names can be passed as bare names (dm, ae) or as quoted strings ("dm", "ae"); both forms are accepted. Lookup against the directory is case-insensitive for both stem and extension, so ks_get_data(dm) and ks_get_data(DM) match any of dm.xpt, DM.XPT, Dm.Xpt, etc.

When type = "auto" (default), the function scans the directory for files matching the requested domains and determines the format from the extension of the first match. All requested domains must use the same format.

The default search path is read from getOption("path.data", "."). Set this option in .Rprofile to avoid repeating the path in every call:

options(path.data = "/my/project/data")

For .xpt (SAS XPORT) files, the reader is selected by the xpt_reader argument (default from option kstools.xpt.reader, fallback "haven"):

"haven"

(default) use haven::read_xpt().

"internal"

use the package-internal ks_read_xpt() parser. This avoids the “ignored N trailing byte(s) after row parsing” warning emitted by haven on some XPORT files. For multi-member XPORT files, the domain slot will contain a named list of tibbles (one per member).

When two or more files in path share the same stem but differ only in case (e.g. both dm.xpt and DM.xpt exist), the resolution strategy is controlled by the global option kstools.get_data.case:

"error"

(default) abort with a message listing the candidates.

"first"

pick the first match in alphabetical order.

"lower"

require the all-lowercase name to exist; otherwise abort.

"upper"

require the all-uppercase name to exist; otherwise abort.

See also

ks_batch_load, read.csv3

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## Load a single domain
options(path.data = "/project/data")
dm <- ks_get_data(dm)

## Case-insensitive lookup: works whether folder has dm.xpt or DM.XPT
dm <- ks_get_data(DM)

## Load multiple domains: returns a named list
dat <- ks_get_data(dm, ae, lb, path = "/project/data/xpt")
head(dat$dm)

## Force a specific file type
dm <- ks_get_data(dm, path = "/project/data", type = "xpt")

## Resolve case-duplicate filenames
options(kstools.get_data.case = "lower")  # prefer dm.xpt over DM.xpt
dm <- ks_get_data(dm, path = "/project/data")

## Quoted strings are also accepted
dat <- ks_get_data("dm", "ae", path = "/project/data")

## Use the internal XPT reader to avoid haven's trailing-byte warning
options(kstools.xpt.reader = "internal")
dm <- ks_get_data(dm, type = "xpt")

## Or override per call without changing the global option
dm <- ks_get_data(dm, type = "xpt", xpt_reader = "internal")
} # }
